title: These Fragile Lives

beats.what: Ultrasound reveals nothing -- Kristi declares no visible fetus; Fatima refuses to accept it and leaves in distress
Victor spends the night screaming at his Jasper doll, demanding it speak; Boyd's father Henry witnesses the breakdown
Donna tells Boyd that given two possibilities -- supernatural or psychological -- she cannot let Fatima and Ellis stay at Colony House
Randall teaches Julie to drive the Colony House van; she finds ruins in the woods that make the hair on their necks stand up
New arrival Dani Acosta confronts Boyd about her confiscated gun; Boyd returns it unloaded and sets a boundary
Fatima stabs Tillie with shears in the greenhouse; episode ends on her screaming at Ellis over what she has done

character_beats.beat: wants to be believed that something real is growing inside her; is dismissed by medical fact -- then the force inside her acts out anyway, bypassing her will entirely
oscillates between protecting Fatima and protecting the community; his compromise (keep the secret, move them out) satisfies neither and plants the episode's crisis
has reversed from decades of endurance into acute desperation; his father's arrival unlocked something he cannot put back

key_lines.line: Why is my point of view the only one everybody assumes is wrong?
key_lines.why: Fatima articulates the injustice at the center of her arc

key_lines.line: If there's nothing there, if the baby isn't real, that means that it's me.
key_lines.why: The epistemological trap: either something horrible is real, or she is broken

key_lines.line: I was so busy taking care of my dad that I was just...
key_lines.why: Tillie's quiet reveal of her own grief; sets up her death 25 minutes later

key_lines.line: You either adapt or you lose your mind.
key_lines.why: Tillie's philosophy -- ironically her final advice before the killing

key_lines.line: Ellis, what have I done? What have I done?!
key_lines.why: Final line; closes the episode on Fatima's horror at her own hand

open_loops: Tillie is dead -- stabbed by Fatima; the community does not yet know who did it or why
The ruins in the woods gave both Randall and Julie a physical sensation; what are they and what happens if Julie goes back?
Boyd's Parkinson's episode mid-search is the first time it has visibly impaired him -- is this accelerating?
Is the entity inside Fatima acting with independent intent to protect itself?

payoffs.what: Jade's bottle-number theory pays off: Jim finds the settlement and begins working the numbers in earnest
Ultrasound machine from ambulance is used; confirms no fetus visible, forcing the psychosomatic-vs-supernatural fork

contradiction.wants: to protect both Fatima and the community, keeping everyone safe
contradiction.does: chooses community safety over Fatima's needs by arranging her removal from Colony House -- a decision that removes the medical proximity that might have contained the crisis

tone_notes: Two major silence blocks: 116 seconds at the 4-6 minute mark (immediately after the ultrasound result lands) and 65 seconds around minute 17 (between Fatima's breakdown and Victor's breakdown) create back-to-back wells of dread. Density spikes at minutes 3-4 (200 wpm) and 43-44 (175 wpm) correspond to the ultrasound confrontation and the greenhouse attack run-up. The episode is the fastest in the batch at 88.1 wpm, matching escalation.
